title: Those bhikkhus, bhikkhus, who are deceitful, stubborn, talkative, fraudulent, haughty, and unconcentrated — those bhikkhus are not my bhikkhus. Those bhikkhus have fallen away from…
content: Those bhikkhus, bhikkhus, who are deceitful, stubborn, talkative, fraudulent, haughty, and unconcentrated — those bhikkhus are not my bhikkhus. Those bhikkhus have fallen away from this Dhamma and Discipline. And they do not achieve growth, increase, or expansion in this Dhamma and Discipline. And those bhikkhus, bhikkhus, who are not deceitful, not talkative, wise, not stubborn, well-concentrated — those bhikkhus are indeed my bhikkhus. Those bhikkhus have not fallen away from this Dhamma and Discipline, and they achieve growth, increase, and expansion in this Dhamma and Discipline.

title: Bhikkhus, there are these three taints. What three? The taint of sensual desire, the taint of existence, and the taint of ignorance. Bhikkhus, these are…
content:
Bhikkhus, there are these three taints. What three? The taint of sensual desire, the taint of existence, and the taint of ignorance. Bhikkhus, these are the three taints.

One who has abandoned the taint of sensual desire,
And the taint of ignorance,
Who has destroyed the taint of existence,
Is liberated from all attachments.
Bearing his final body,
He has conquered Māra and his host.

title: ( Blessed One ): For one without anger, Whence does anger come? Living tamed, with right livelihood, Liberated, through right knowledge. That one lives thus,…
content:
( Blessed One ):
For one without anger,
Whence does anger come?
Living tamed, with right livelihood,
Liberated, through right knowledge.
That one lives thus,
A life of peace.
Those who, when reviled,
Revile in return,
Do evil to themselves,
And also evil to others.
Those who, when reviled,
Do not revile in return,
That person wins a battle,
A victory for both self and other.
That one seeks the benefit
Of both self and other.
And the one who reviled,
Understanding, calms down.
A physician to both,
Healing self and healing other,
People think him a fool,
Because they do not understand the Dhamma.

title: Furthermore, householders, a noble disciple reflects: 'If someone were to break up my friends by divisive speech, that would be undesirable and unpleasing for me.…
content: Furthermore, householders, a noble disciple reflects: 'If someone were to break up my friends by divisive speech, that would be undesirable and unpleasing for me. But if I were to break up another's friends by divisive speech, that would be undesirable and unpleasing for that person. This state that is undesirable and unpleasing for me is also undesirable and unpleasing for others. Since this state is undesirable and unpleasing for me, why should I impose it on others?' Reflecting thus, he himself abstains from divisive speech, encourages others to abstain from divisive speech, and speaks in praise of abstaining from divisive speech. Thus, in verbal conduct, he becomes completely pure.

title: 'A transgression has overcome me, Venerable Sir, foolish, deluded, and unwholesome as I am. For while the Blessed One was teaching the bhikkhus a Dhamma…
content: 'A transgression has overcome me, Venerable Sir, foolish, deluded, and unwholesome as I am. For while the Blessed One was teaching the bhikkhus a Dhamma talk connected with the training, encouraging, inspiring, and gladdening them, I felt impatient and displeased, thinking: 'This samaṇa is too meticulous.' Venerable Sir, may the Blessed One accept my transgression as a transgression, so that I may restrain myself in the future.' - 'Indeed, Kassapogotta, a transgression has overcome you, foolish, deluded, and unwholesome as you are. For while I was teaching the bhikkhus a Dhamma talk connected with the training, encouraging, inspiring, and gladdening them, you felt impatient and displeased, thinking: 'This samaṇa is too meticulous.' And, Kassapogotta, since you see your transgression as a transgression and make amends according to the Dhamma, I accept your confession. This is growth in the Noble One's Discipline, that one sees a transgression as a transgression, makes amends according to the Dhamma, and restrains oneself in the future.'

title: The brahmin Asurindaka Bhāradvāja heard: 'The brahmin of the Bhāradvāja clan has gone forth under the Blessed One, from home to homelessness.' Angry and displeased,…
content:
The brahmin Asurindaka Bhāradvāja heard: 'The brahmin of the Bhāradvāja clan has gone forth under the Blessed One, from home to homelessness.' Angry and displeased, he went to the Blessed One and, having arrived, reviled and abused the Blessed One with rude, harsh words. Hearing this, the Blessed One remained silent. Then the brahmin Asurindaka Bhāradvāja said to the Blessed One: 'You are defeated, samaṇa! You are defeated, samaṇa!'

( Blessed One ):
'The fool thinks he wins
When he speaks harsh words.
One who knows how to endure
That one truly wins.

Those who, when reviled,
Revile in return,
Do evil to themselves,
And also evil to others.
Those who, when reviled,
Do not revile in return,
That person has won a battle,
A victory for both self and other.

That one seeks the benefit
Of both self and other.
And the one who reviled,
Understanding, calms down.

A physician to both,
Healing self and healing other,
People think him a fool,
Because they do not understand the Dhamma.'

title: 'Damsels in assembly gather, Ghosts come and go, That forest is called the forest of delusion, How can there be an escape?' ( Blessed One…
content:
'Damsels in assembly gather,
Ghosts come and go,
That forest is called the forest of delusion,
How can there be an escape?'

( Blessed One ):
'That path is called the straight path,
That direction is called fearless,
The chariot is called noiseless,
Fitted with the Dhamma-wheel.

Conscience is the chariot's leaning-board,
Mindfulness is its canopy,
I say the charioteer
Is the true Dhamma,
And right view itself
Goes quickly ahead.'

Whether a man or a woman,
Both use that chariot.
By means of that chariot,
They go towards Nibbāna.

title: The merit of a giver Always increases, He overcomes hatred, Does not store up restraint. A good person abandons All evil, unwholesome deeds, Destroys greed,…
content:
The merit of a giver
Always increases,
He overcomes hatred,
Does not store up restraint.

A good person abandons
All evil, unwholesome deeds,
Destroys greed, hatred, delusion.
His mind is liberated, pure.

title: 'For their whole life, the Arahants have abandoned non-celibacy, live the celibate life, live aloof, abstain from the vulgar practice of sexual intercourse. Today, this…
content: 'For their whole life, the Arahants have abandoned non-celibacy, live the celibate life, live aloof, abstain from the vulgar practice of sexual intercourse. Today, this night and this day, I also abandon non-celibacy, live the celibate life, live aloof, abstain from the vulgar practice of sexual intercourse. By this factor, following the example of the Arahants, I will observe the uposatha day.'

title: Questioner: He with open eyes has clearly declared The Dhamma that can be known, overcoming all dangers. Please, O good one, explain the path, Or…
content:
Questioner:
He with open eyes has clearly declared
The Dhamma that can be known, overcoming all dangers.
Please, O good one, explain the path,
Or about specific liberation, or about jhāna.

The Blessed One:
Do not be greedy for forms!
Block your ears to the noise of the village!
Do not be attached to tastes!
Let nothing in the world be considered 'mine'!

When contacted by contacts, let a bhikkhu not lament over anything.
Let him not long for any kind of existence,
And let him not tremble in the face of terrors.

Having obtained food and drink, solid food and clothing,
Let him not hoard them; if he does not obtain them, let him not be anxious.

Let him practice jhāna, not wandering about,
Not delighting in restlessness, not falling into heedlessness.
Let him dwell in silent lodgings, in seats and beds.

Let him sleep little, be wakeful, ardent,
Abandon laziness, deceit, laughter, play,
Sexual intercourse, and all adornments.

Let him not tremble when blamed,
Nor be elated when praised.
Let him abandon greed, stinginess, anger, and divisive speech.

Let him not engage in buying and selling,
Nor criticize anyone anywhere.
Let him not be angry in the village,
Nor, for the sake of gain, talk with people.

Let a bhikkhu not speak boastfully,
Nor speak with an ulterior motive.
Let him not train in insolence,
Nor utter provocative words.

Let him not be led into false speech,
Nor intentionally do deceitful things.
Let him not despise others for their life,
Their wisdom, or their virtue.

Having heard harsh words from ascetics or ordinary people,
Let him not respond with harsh words;
The peaceful, gentle one does not retaliate.

Knowing this Dhamma, a bhikkhu should train
Mindfully, always comprehending.
Knowing the state of peace, he is called 'calmed'.
Do not be heedless in Gotama's teaching.

He who is victorious is not defeated;
He sees the Dhamma for himself, not by hearsay.
Therefore, always train heedfully
With respect for the Blessed One's teaching.
